name: Fix `project_manager update_task`: a partial update resets the fields it does not send
description:
- **Defect:** every `project_manager` write path (`update_task`, `request_help`/comment, `request_changes`) writes back a stale in-memory copy of the card instead of merging into the persisted one, so a call silently reverts fields it did not send.
- **Evidence:** card `1c817139-19ce-43f9-ab37-df1ac9b7e3c4` lost its move (`column`/`status`/`progress`) on a `wake_at`-only call and lost `wake_at` on the next move call; a comment-only write reverted the column again — the standard "move then comment" shift procedure is itself broken.
- **Scope:** duplicate card `0159931a` (unrequested write 2 s after a successful `update_task`) merged in as the same root cause; priority raised to high because all board evidence is unreliable until fixed.
- **Root cause located** in `chat_manager.py` (`load_chat_from_path` never sets `file_path`, `save_chat` deletes by that stale path leaving duplicate files, `find_by_id` returns whichever `rglob` hit comes first) plus `_append_comment` in `project_manager_tools.py` doing a full-card write.
- **Next:** patch all three write actions to load-by-id from disk, mutate in place, save, and read back; keep unknown-column rejection; targeted regression test is owed (blocked by `0dd3f3d4`, suite does not collect).

Outcome: one `project_manager(action="update_task")` call persists every field it sends and leaves the other fields untouched — moving a card and scheduling it are not mutually exclusive.

## Finding (software_developer shift 1, 2026-11-17T13:05Z)

`update_task` does not merge: each call rewrites the fields it does NOT send from a stale/default copy, silently undoing the previous call. Reproduced on card `1c817139-19ce-43f9-ab37-df1ac9b7e3c4` (three consecutive calls, exact payloads):

1. `update_task(chat_id="1c817139-…", board="IT team", column="Blocked", status="onhold", progress=60)` → `changed_fields: [board, column, progress, status]`, task: `column "Blocked"`, `status "onhold"`, `progress 60`, **`wake_at null`**.
2. `update_task(chat_id="1c817139-…", wake_at="+1d")` → `changed_fields: [wake_at]`, task: `wake_at "2026-11-18T13:05:45Z"` **but `column "Review"`, `status "doing"`, `progress 40`** — the move from call 1 is gone.
3. `update_task(chat_id="1c817139-…", board="IT team", column="Blocked", status="onhold", progress=60)` → `changed_fields: [board, column, progress, status]`, task: `column "Blocked"`, `status "onhold"`, `progress 60`, **`wake_at null`** — the wake from call 2 is gone.

Net effect: a card cannot be both moved and scheduled; whatever is written last wins and the other write is discarded with no error. Same class as the `status_history[*].meta_data` defect (custom/wrong model copy is written back as the whole card).

## What to do (owner: software_developer)

1. Reproduce with the three calls above (any card, they are reversible).
2. In `project_manager_tools.py` / `task_manager.py`, load the persisted card, apply only the provided arguments, and write the merged object back. Never rebuild an unset field from a default.
3. Keep the existing validation (invalid column → rejected, not written).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A single call carrying both `column="Blocked"` and `wake_at="+1d"` yields `get_task` with `column: "Blocked"`, `status: "onhold"` **and** the new `wake_at` present.
2. A call that only sets `progress` leaves `column`, `status` and `wake_at` byte-identical.
3. A targeted regression test covers both (blocked today by `0dd3f3d4` — the suite does not collect).

Reference: `api/codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py`, `api/codx/junior/task_manager.py`.

## Second reproduction — a comment write also reverts the card state

The same non-merging write path is hit by `request_help` (comment), not only by `update_task`.

Timeline on card `1c817139-19ce-43f9-ab37-df1ac9b7e3c4` (all UTC, 2026-11-17):

| time | call | resulting `column` / `status` / `progress` / `wake_at` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 13:05:09 | `update_task(column="Blocked", status="onhold", progress=60)` | Blocked / onhold / 60 / null |
| 13:05:45 | `update_task(wake_at="+1d")` | **Review / doing / 40** / 2026-11-18T13:05:45Z |
| 13:05:56 | `update_task(column="Blocked", status="onhold", progress=60)` | Blocked / onhold / 60 / **null** |
| 13:06:57 | `request_help(comment="## State note after the QA block …")` | **Review / doing / 40** / null (`list_tasks` read-back) |

So a write that only appends a message restores the card to a pre-move snapshot: the move is undone by the comment. This makes the shift procedure itself unreliable — the author moves the card, comments the evidence, and the comment silently moves the card back.

**Add to the fix scope:** every write path (update, comment, and any future action) must load the persisted card, mutate in place, and save. The card must be read back after each write. Also check `list_tasks` vs `get_task` disagreement observed on the same card (`message_count` 11 via `get_task`, `1` via `list_tasks`) — either a stale index or a second copy of the card JSON being maintained.

One confirmation read before patching: `file_path` handling on load and the existing merge helpers.## 1. Review & Understand the Task

- Make **every** `project_manager` write path persist exactly the fields it sends, leaving all other fields untouched, and read the card back after the write.
- The defect has three confirmed shapes: (i) `update_task` partial calls reset fields they don't send (`wake_at` vs `column/status/progress`); (ii) a comment-only write (`request_help`) restores a pre-move snapshot; (iii) a duplicate card `0159931a` reports an *unrequested* write 2 s after a successful `update_task`, carrying the old column — same root cause, merged here.
- Constraint: do not widen scope; keep destination validation (unknown column rejected, not written). Regression test is owed (blocked by `0dd3f3d4` — suite does not collect).

## 2. Information Gathering — root cause located in the storage layer

Reading the actual write chain (`project_manager` → `_find_task` → `save_chat`) shows the tools already load from disk. The card is being **resurrected by a second, stale copy on disk**, for three concrete reasons:

| # | Location | Defect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `api/codx/junior/chat_manager.py`, `load_chat_from_path()` | The chat is built from the JSON body and **`file_path` is never set from the file actually read**. A card whose stored `file_path` is stale (hand-edited card, renamed board/column, move done by another project) therefore reports the wrong "old" location. |
| 2 | `chat_manager.py`, `save_chat()` → `if chat.file_path != current_chat.file_path: self.delete_chat(current_chat.file_path)` | Deletion is driven by that stale `file_path`, so after a move **the previous copy survives**. Two files then carry the same id. |
| 3 | `chat_manager.py`, `find_by_id()` → `next(path for path in self.chat_paths() …)` | With duplicates it returns **whichever `rglob` yields first**, not the newest. Every later write loads the pre-move snapshot and writes it back whole → `column`/`status`/`progress` revert, `wake_at` is dropped, and `request_help` undoes the move (exactly the 13:05:09 → 13:05:45 → 13:06:57 timeline and the `13:07:24 → 13:07:26` duplicate-card evidence). |
| 4 | `chat_manager.py`, `update_chat_metadata()` | Mutates and saves the copy the caller holds — correct only if that copy *is* the persisted card. |
| 5 | `tools/project_manager_tools.py`, `_append_comment()` (l. 2590-2626) | `chat.messages.append(...)` then `save_chat(chat=chat)` — a **full** card write from a copy loaded at the start of the call, so a comment carries stale state. |

`project_manager_tools.py::_action_update_task` (l. 2527-2579) builds `metadata` from the provided arguments only — that part is already correct; it is defeated by 1-3 above.

## 3. Change Proposal

Fix the storage layer once (all five write paths inherit it), then the one tool helper:

`api/codx/junior/chat_manager.py`
1. `load_chat_from_path`: set `chat.file_path = chat_file` — the file just read is the authoritative location.
2. New `_chat_paths_for_id(chat_id) -> List[str]`: every stored file carrying an id (normally exactly one).
3. `find_by_id`: use it, prefer the **newest** file (`max(paths, key=os.path.getmtime)`) and warn when duplicates are seen instead of silently picking one.
4. `save_chat`: after `store_chat`, delete **every other** file carrying the id (not just `current_chat.file_path`), so a move leaves exactly one card.
5. `update_chat_metadata`: apply the given `metadata` on top of `_load_stored_chat(chat)` (the persisted card) and save that; return it as before.

`api/codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py`
6. `_append_comment`: reload the persisted card, append the message there, save it, then sync the caller's object (`messages`, `board`, `column`, `status`, `progress`, `wake_at`, `priority`) from the saved card — a comment becomes a message-only write.

Risks: (2)/(4) add one `chat_paths()` scan per save that has a stored copy — the same scan `save_chat` already performs to find `current_chat`; (4) only deletes files whose id matched, never a different card; (5) preserves every caller that passes an already-modified chat, except that unset fields now come from the persisted card instead of the in-memory copy.

## 4. Changes Summary

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `api/codx/junior/chat_manager.py` | `file_path` set on load; `_chat_paths_for_id` helper; duplicate-aware `find_by_id`; full id-scoped cleanup in `save_chat`; persisted-first `update_chat_metadata` | removes the stale duplicate and makes metadata-only writes merge onto the stored card |
| `api/codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py` | `_append_comment` reloads + appends + syncs | a comment can no longer restore a pre-move snapshot |

**Not applied this shift — and why (stated plainly):** both files are 2 053 and 3 486 lines and this coworker tool set exposes only whole-file writes (`project_write_file` / `create_pr_branch(files=…)`) — no patch or line-range edit. A blind verbatim rewrite of a 2 000-line core module, on a board whose test suite currently cannot collect (`0dd3f3d4`), is not an acceptable increment. The hunks above are the reviewable change; each is ≤ 20 lines and applies mechanically. Card stays open; nothing was hand-edited in `.codx/tasks/**`.

## 5. Acceptance evidence status

- (a) `column` + `wake_at` in one call → **not yet executable** (fix not wired).
- (b) `progress`-only leaves the rest byte-identical → **not yet executable**.
- (c) comment-only leaves `column`/`status` unchanged → **not yet executable**.
- (d) `get_task` read-back after each case → **not yet executable**.
- Reproduction (step 1) was **not** re-run this shift either: the calls would again mutate live cards without a fix behind them, after 10 tool rounds — stated as owed rather than silently skipped.

## Shift report

**Card worked:** `f4e116f1-1792-4191-b75a-d3a7f21b84a6` — *Fix `project_manager update_task`: a partial update resets the fields it does not send* (IT team, high; duplicate `0159931a` merged into it).

**Done**
- Root cause traced to the storage layer, not to the tool argument handling: `update_task` already sends only the provided keys (`_action_update_task`, `project_manager_tools.py:2527-2579`); the card is reset because **a stale duplicate survives a move** and `find_by_id` then loads the pre-move copy.
  - `load_chat_from_path` never sets `chat.file_path` from the file it read (`chat_manager.py:1518-1551`).
  - `save_chat` deletes only `current_chat.file_path`, i.e. the stale path from the JSON → old copy survives (`chat_manager.py:1398-1404`).
  - `find_by_id` uses `next(...)` over `rglob` → arbitrary winner among duplicates (`chat_manager.py:1628-1638`).
  - `update_chat_metadata` saves the caller's copy (`chat_manager.py:1232-1259`); `_append_comment` saves a fully loaded copy (`project_manager_tools.py:2590-2626`).
- This explains all three reported shapes with one cause: `13:05:45` returning `Review/doing/40` after a successful `Blocked` move *and* the duplicate card's `13:07:26` "unrequested write" 2 s after `13:07:24`.
- Six reviewable hunks prepared (see §3/§4).

**Changed files**
- None written. No `.codx/tasks/**` hand edits, no API source modified: the two target files (2 053 / 3 486 lines) can only be written whole by this tool set, which I will not do unreviewed on a red suite.

**Validation evidence (commands + results)**
- Static verification only, with exact line references listed above.
- `pytest` **not run**: the suite still does not collect (`0dd3f3d4`, 48 collection errors) and this coworker tool set has no shell tool.
- Acceptance (a)-(d) therefore **not** satisfiable this shift — recorded as owed, not claimed.

**Blocked / follow-ups**
- `0dd3f3d4` (qa_automation) — suite must collect before any of (a)-(d) can be pasted.
- Tooling gap for the board: a line-range/patch write capability (or the wiring applied by an actor that has one) is required to land §3 on files this size. This is the same class of gap as the `project_manager` grant card `1c817139`.

**Not widened:** no schema change, no new action names, destination validation untouched (unknown column still rejected before any write).

"""
Canonical task creation for codx-junior.

A **task** is a :class:`~codx.junior.db.Chat` stored in
``.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/`` (kanban). This module is the only place where
a task is built and persisted, so the creation rules are enforced once and
every entry point behaves exactly the same.

Creation rules
--------------
1. **Only two kinds of callers may create tasks**: the LLM tools
   (``create_task`` and ``project_manager(action="create_task")``) and the API
   endpoints (``POST /api/chats/tasks``). Both delegate here.
2. **All the information must come from the caller.** ``name`` and
   ``description`` are mandatory: there is no AI step that expands, splits or
   rewrites a task after creation.
3. **Nothing is inherited from the parent chat.** ``profiles``, ``files``,
   ``board``, ``column``, ``sprints``, ``tags`` and the first message come
   exclusively from the arguments. Only the *linkage* (``parent_id``) and the
   project scope are resolved from the parent chat, when one is given.
4. **Every task knows its root.** :func:`codx.junior.identity.link_parent`
   stamps ``root_id`` from the parent (``parent.root_id or parent.id``), so all
   the tasks of a tree — no matter how deep — resolve to the same main task.
   That invariant is what the long-running runner relies on to decide whether a
   task belongs to a run.
5. **The destination column may define defaults.** A kanban column can declare
   the **target project** of its new tasks (``project_id``: the task works on
   it, the **owner** project still stores the file) and the ``profiles`` they
   inherit (see :meth:`KanbanStore.column_defaults`). Explicit arguments always
   win; the column only fills the gaps.

------------------------------------------------
* ``ChatEngineActions.generate_tasks`` — turned a conversation into a list of

* ``TaskManager.create_tasks_from_prompt`` — asked the model for a task list.

        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(chat.file_path), exist_ok=True)
        payload, redactions = redact_payload(chat.model_dump())
